processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Plates with dimensions 90 mm × 40 mm × 20 mm sectioned from the 10 kg induction-melted ingot were first homogenized at 1050 °C for 1 h.

processing_steps.method: hot rolling followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After homogenization the plates were hot-rolled to a thickness of 3 mm (from 20 mm, i.e. 85% reduction per the Figure 1a schematic) and immediately water-quenched to room temperature.
Hot-rolled sheets were cold-rolled to a final thickness of approximately 1.5 mm; single-pass reduction rate ≤5%, corresponding to a total thickness reduction of 50%.

processing_steps.method: solution treatment followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The cold-rolled sheet was solution-treated at 900 °C for 15 min, followed by water quenching, yielding the austenite + B2 duplex microstructure with VC and L'12 LRO nanoprecipitates. This is the terminal state of the studied sample.

structures.overall_structure: Austenite–B2 duplex microstructure with dual-nanoprecipitation inside the austenite: Ni/Al-enriched B2 phase coexisting with austenite, with VC carbides and L'12-type long-range ordered (LRO) domains dispersed within the austenite. XRD/phase-diagram/EBSD phase fractions are consistent.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: grain-size histogram with Gauss fitting (Figure 2e); mean D̄_γ = 1.31 µm

precipitates.distribution: nanoscale particles within the austenite, impeding dislocation motion; volume fraction 0.26%
homogeneously distributed nanoscale ordered domains within austenite grains; volume fraction 11.10%; irregular shapes

phases_present.volume_fraction: 20% (V_B2 by XRD direct comparison; consistent with equilibrium diagram and EBSD, f_B2 = 20%)
phases_present.morphology: two distinct forms — long strip-like large grains and fine particles decorating austenite grain boundaries

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: bimodal size distribution resolved into two Gauss fittings: D̄_band = 1.02 µm and D̄_particle = 3.38 µm (Figure 2f)
